items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names say what they do (unboundedPreceding, buildWindowSpec, buildWindowClause, Frame). Each .window() has a JSDoc in the house style ('Adds a `window` clause to the query.'). Error messages are clear and formatting matches the existing builders.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: buildWindowClause is shared across dialects, but the name checks (`name.length === 0` / `name.trim().length === 0` with their throws) are copied into all 5 dialect select.ts files instead of a shared assert. window.ts also sits in sql/expressions, not sql/functions as the convention asks.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: preceding()/following() reject negative and non-integer values with the helper name in the message. Frame rejects from > to by comparing offsets and blocks unbounded_following as from. sql.raw only receives validated integers. Window names are validated, and hidden tests pass 130/130.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: Optional `windows?: { name; spec }[]` is added to all 5 *SelectConfig types, with an identical .window() on the pg/mysql/sqlite/gel/singlestore builders. windowSql is empty when no windows are set, so existing SQL is unchanged. Exports are added via expressions/index.ts and P2P passes 566/566.
